sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.06.2011 passed in MVC.No.1300/2002 by Member, MACT, Puttur, D.K, respondent No.2 - Insurance Company therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 06.09.1999 the petitioner along with pillion rider was riding his scooter bearing registration No.KA-21-E-6996 from Kolthige village of Puttur taluk to Puttur town and when he reached a place called Santyar of Aryapu village at about 10.30 a.m., he met with an accident with a KSRTC bus bearing registration KA-09-F-2212.
The bus belonged to respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is the Insurance Company, which had insured the scooter of the petitioner.
4. Initially, the petitioner preferred a petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 of the MV Act.
Later, he amended the petition to the effect that it was filed under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act 1988.

The petitioner have examined four witnesses and has got marked Exs.P1 to P19 and the respondents have not examined any witnesses but have got marked the Insurance policy of the petitioner's scooter as Ex.R1.
The respondents in their written statement have denied their respective liability.

The Tribunal based on the pleadings and evidence let in has awarded a compensation of Rs.88,714/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and has directed respondent No.2 - Insurance company (insurer of petitioner's scooter)
to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, respondent No.2 has preferred this appeal.
5. The case of respondent No.2 is that it had issued a package/ comprehensive policy to the scooter of the petitioner.
But no premium was collected towards the personal accident benefit of the insured.
It is submitted that the insurance policy covered only the risk against the third parties and own damage to the vehicle insured.
Under the circumstances, it is submitted that if there is any liability, the same has to be fastened on respondent No.1 - KSRTC.
6. The petitioner though served has remained absent.

7. Respondent No.1 - KSRTC submits that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Shri Guddappa Gowda on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41022805/
2 of the scooter and there was no fault on the KSRTC driver and hence it is not liable to compensate the petitioner.

sentences.text: However, respondent No.1 does not dispute the fact that the insurance policy issued by respondent No.2 - insurance company is a comprehensive policy and it does not show any premium being collected towards personal accident coverage of the driver - owner of the vehicle.
8. In the impugned order, the Tribunal has concluded that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the scooter and not the KSRTC bus.
However, on the ground that a comprehensive insurance policy covers the injury to the owner, respondent No.2 has been made liable to compensate the petitioner.
9. The petition itself is filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'Act') as it stood then.

The same reads as mentioned hereunder:
163A.

Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section(1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicle concerned or of any other person.
(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule.
Thus, in a claim petition filed under Section 163A of the Act, the claimant is not required to prove negligence on part of the alleged offending vehicle.
Mere involvement of the vehicle in question in the accident is sufficient.
In the instant case, there is no dispute as to the two vehicles which are involved in the accident.

The petitioner has suffered the following injuries in the accident:
Lacerated wound on the face, upper eyelid, over chin, and x-ray revealed united fracture ofsub trochantic region of femur with implant in site and new bone formation over the region of greater trochanter.
The said injuries are grievous in nature.
10. The question that now arises for consideration is as to which of the respondent is liable to pay compensation.

Reading of exhibit R1, makes it clear that it is a comprehensive insurance policy,
covering any injuries to the third parties concerned and own damage to the vehicle insured.
But as there is no premium collected towards personal accident coverage, any injury to the rider - owner, in this case the petitioner, is not covered.

The Apex Court in the case of DHANRAJ VS. NEW INDIA The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Shri Guddappa Gowda on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41022805/
3 ASSURANCE CO., LTD., AND ANOTHER., reported in 2005 ACJ 1 in paragraph Nos. 9 and 10 have held as under:
"9. In the case of Oriental Insurance. Co., Ltd., Vs.Sunita Rathi, 1998 ACJ 121 (SC), it has been held that the liability of an insurance company is only for the purpose of indemnifying the insured against liabilities incurred towards third person or in respect of damages to property.

sentences.text: Thus, where the insured, i.e., an owner of the vehicle has no liability to a third party the insurance company has no liability also.
10. In this case, it has not been shown that the policy covered any risk for injury to the owner himself.
We are unable to accept the contention that the premium of Rs.4,989/- paid under the heading 'own damage' is for covering liability towards personal injury.
Under the heading 'own damage', the words 'premium on vehicle and non- electrical accessories' appear.
It is thus clear that this premium is towards damage to the vehicle and not for injury to the person of the owner.
An owner of a vehicle can only claim provided a personal accident insurance has been taken out.
In this case, there is no such insurance."
Thus, in the instant case, respondent No.2 cannot be made liable to the injuries of the petitioner.
11. In respect of respondent No.1, the Tribunal based on the evidence let in has come to the conclusion that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
The Tribunal based on the said finding has not held respondent No.1 liable to compensate the petitioner.
However, the Tribunal has erred in not considering the fact that the claim petition was filed under Section 163A of the Act, and it does not require any negligence to be proved against a person.
The bus of respondent No.1 was insured against the third party risks by way of internal insurance fund.

That means, when a claim is made against the first respondent under the provisions of Section 163A of the Act, by any person, on the ground that he met with an accident with the bus belonging to respondent No.1 - KSRTC, the first respondent cannot deny its liability.
The advocate for respondent No.1 is not in a position to contravene the said proposition.
12. Thus, under the present facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal has fixed the liability on first respondent and not the second respondent.
13. The next question that arises for consideration is whether is quantum fixed by the Tribunal is appropriate or not ?
14. As per the provision of 163A of the Act, the compensation has to be calculated as per the provisions of II Schedule of the Act as it existed then.
It is seen the Tribunal has erred in calculating the quantum of compensation also.
15. As per the II Schedule the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,000/- for sustaining grievous injuries.
The tribunal has taken his income at Rs.3,000/- per month and thereby his annual income would be Rs.36,000/-.

He was aged 62 years at the time of the accident and thus a The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Shri Guddappa Gowda on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41022805/
4 multiplier of '5' is adopted.

sentences.text: He has suffered a total body disability of 6% and thereby he would be entitled to a sum of Rs.10,800/- towards disability.
Further, as per the schedule he would be entitled to a maximum sum of Rs.15,000/- towards Medical expenses.
Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.30,800/- as against Rs.88,714/- awarded by the tribunal.
Further, given the bank rate of interest, it would be appropriate to award 6% interest per annum on the said amount of Rs.30,800/- from the date of petition before the tribunal till realization.

16. Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.

ii. The compensation payable is reduced to Rs.30,800/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of the petition before the Tribunal till realization and respondent No.1 - KSRTC shall be liable to compensate the - 10 - petitioner within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iii. Amount-in-deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the tribunal, which shall be refunded to respondent No.2 - appellant herein.
